IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: The method of production of a Standard by either CENELEC or IEC is outlined in relation to specifications for low- and medium-voltage cable accessories, joints, indoor and outdoor terminations and separable connectors. Other tasks engaging Working Group 11 of CENELEC Technical Committee 20 are listed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: That looks too simple; it'll never work! (cable accessory materials)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: Modern materials such as cold pour resins, cold shrink systems, moulded rubber components and new tapes with specialised electrical properties have been introduced. In conjunction with new mechanical connecting systems, they have gradually replaced the traditional techniques, with resulting reduction in installation times. The design philosophies behind modern 3M accessories are explained. The important electrical and mechanical properties of the modern materials are discussed and the reasoning behind their choice within accessories is explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cold pour resins in MV cable joints
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: Joint designs are categorised according to the electrical duty that the resin performs. Problems to be avoided with modern jointing resins are considered, and the advantages of resin encapsulation are enumerated, with line drawings of typical resin-insulated, non-resin-insulated and composite joints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Users' experience of 11 kV distribution cable accessories
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: This paper is a brief review of two regional electricity companies' experience of 11 kV jointing systems and accessories introduced during the last 10 years. The two companies, Hydro-Electric and Seeboard, supply customers at the opposite ends of the UK, and a comparison of the statistics gives an indication of the network mix and the type of territories in which they supply. Both companies employ mechanical sheath clamps and heat shrink cable entry seals to terminate PICAS cable. The design of this type of termination has evolved to match the reliability of traditional bitumen-filled terminations. Advantages of these new terminations are discussed together with those of resin-insulated and cold shrink counterparts. Susceptibility to jointer error, especially with paper insulated cables is highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: The author briefly outlines some problems associated with replacing soldered phase conductor connections and terminations by mechanical bolt or shear bolt connectors. The comments are concerned mainly with the problems, and solutions, of replacing soldered connections at 11 and 33 kV, and cover oil impregnated paper insulated stranded conductors (both shaped and circular), polymeric insulated circular compacted stranded conductors and polymeric insulated solid aluminium conductors (circular and shaped). The target is to match the performance of the soldered sweated connection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Material progress towards a modern accessory system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: The ability of polymeric materials to perform as high voltage insulation is now beyond question. The last quarter century has seen rapid development of polymer compositions for insulators, cables and cable accessories. The technology of conferring on chosen polymers the necessary functional characteristics is now well understood and there can be confidence that the electricity supply industry target of 40 years service life can be readily achieved with the right materials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: The development of polymeric insulated cables for medium voltage applications has led quite naturally to the demand for a matching range of accessories in order to take full advantage of the 'dry' cable philosophy. Accessories utilising the cold jointing solution by means of stretch rubber techniques and methods of application are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: It's easy, anyone can do it! (cable jointing technology)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Cable Accessories up to 33kV
abstract: The technical complexity of modern cable accessories (connectors, joints and terminations) and their susceptibility to errors in assembly are highlighted. Experience with training courses and seminars for jointing operators and their supervisors is recounted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
